name: Techstars Boston
desc: The storied global accelerator's Boston program â€” mentor-driven, 13 weeks, $220K standard deal.
why: The classic accelerator brand with a deep Boston mentor bench.

name: NextView Ventures
desc: Seed-stage fund focused on 'redesigning the everyday economy' â€” backing founders using software and AI to solve mass-market problems.
why: Boston-native since 2010. Writes $500Kâ€“$2M checks at seed. Notable exit: Hatch acquired by Yelp for $300M (2026).
facts: Everyday economy â€” software and AI

name: GC Venture Fellowship (fka Rough Draft Ventures)
desc: General Catalyst's student-focused venture arm â€” invests exclusively in student and recent-graduate founders.
why: The earliest entry point for MIT/Harvard AI founders. $25Kâ€“$100K checks. Critical pipeline for academic spinouts before they're on anyone else's radar.

name: MassVentures
desc: The Commonwealth's own venture arm â€” START grants and early capital for MA deep-tech startups.
why: Non-dilutive state grants: $100K at Round 1, $200K at Round 2, then up to $500K of Round 3 seed capital in a spinout. Needs an SBIR/STTR Phase II; the window reopens Feb 1, 2027. MV Accelerate adds free SBIR coaching and Founders School.

name: FoundersEdge
desc: Pre-seed fund writing $100â€“$200K first checks into AI-native, software-first B2B startups, run by post-exit operators Greg Raiz (Raizlabs, Techstars Boston) and Jess Lynch (Wishroute).
why: Operator GPs who lead or co-invest without taking a board seat, plus a CEO peer cohort and open demo nights like Ditch the Deck â€” first-check money that comes with hands-on company.

name: Innospark Ventures
desc: Boston seed fund investing only where AI is the core product â€” applied AI and deep tech across healthcare, life sciences and enterprise; checks typically $1Mâ€“$3M.
why: Run by a repeat AI founder and backs nothing but AI companies â€” as on-thesis as Boston seed money gets.
facts: AI-core only: health, life sci, enterprise

name: First Star Ventures
desc: Cambridge pre-seed fund writing $100Kâ€“$1M first checks into AI, robotics and frontier-computing companies; both partners are technical ex-founders.
why: First-check money from two GPs who can read your research â€” they show up before anyone else does.

name: HubSpot Ventures
desc: HubSpot's strategic venture arm â€” $500Kâ€“$5M checks from seed through Series B, focused on AI & agent development and intelligent apps for SMBs; investments include Lovable and ElevenLabs.
why: Strategic capital with distribution: the HubSpot platform and its SMB customer base come with the check.
facts: AI agents and SMB intelligent apps

name: Bain Capital Ventures
desc: Boston-founded multi-stage firm with named AI-apps and AI-infrastructure practices â€” $1â€“5M seed checks through $100M growth rounds, plus the BCV Labs AI incubator.
why: Seed through growth without leaving the cap table, and an AI incubator on top.

name: January Ventures
desc: Woman-led pre-seed fund writing $150Kâ€“$750K checks before product, customers or revenue â€” currently focused on founders transforming healthcare, manufacturing and supply chain with AI.
why: True pre-seed money with an explicit thesis on AI founders from non-traditional backgrounds â€” they invest earlier than almost anyone.
facts: AI in health, manufacturing, supply chain

name: SBXi
desc: Sponsor-backed syndicate writing fast first checks exclusively for MIT-alumni founders â€” $10Kâ€“$100K on SAFEs, up to $1M matching a qualifying term sheet; grew out of the MIT Sandbox program.
why: One of the quickest paths to a first yes for the large MIT-born share of Boston AI startups.
facts: SAFEs; match needs qualifying term sheet

name: Bosch Ventures
desc: Robert Bosch's corporate venture arm, whose Boston-area office anchors its North American enterprise-AI investing â€” a $270M sixth fund writing $5Mâ€“$10M checks, with local investments including Blitzy.
why: Strategic capital plus a route to industrial customers â€” strongest for AI applied to the physical world.

name: MIT delta v
desc: MIT's summer venture accelerator: up to $20K equity-free plus living stipends, ending in a famous September Demo Day.
why: The single best on-ramp for MIT student founders. Zero dilution.

name: MIT Venture Mentoring Service
desc: Free, team-based mentoring from vetted entrepreneurs and executives for MIT-affiliated ventures. No equity, ever.
why: Arguably the most underrated free resource in the ecosystem.

name: Harvard Innovation Labs
desc: Harvard's venture launchpad â€” programming, space and accelerator tracks for student and alumni founders.
why: Free for Harvard affiliates and the President's Innovation Challenge awards $500K+ yearly.

name: The Engine
desc: MIT created this tough-tech hub in 2016; it became an independent 501(c)(3) in 2025, and Engine Ventures spun out as a separate investment firm in 2023. 220,000 sq ft of managed wet lab, engineering and office space, plus Blueprint, a free 8-week mostly virtual program for researchers turning lab work into a company.
why: Lab space and equipment that would otherwise cost millions, for AI that meets hardware, energy or bio. Fee-based and month-to-month, no equity, no MIT affiliation or Engine Ventures funding required. Residency grants can subsidize teams short on cash; the space itself brings no investment.
facts: Applied AI & ML plus 14 tough-tech fields

name: MassRobotics
desc: The world's largest independent robotics innovation hub: shared labs, test space and corporate partners for robotics & physical-AI startups.
why: Embodied-AI founders get equipment, space and intros that nowhere else in the US concentrates this densely.
facts: Shared labs, test space, corp partners

name: Greentown Labs
desc: North America's largest climatetech incubator â€” increasingly home to AI-for-energy and AI-for-climate startups.
why: If your AI serves climate or energy, this is your tribe (and your lab bench).
facts: Climatetech; AI for energy and climate

name: IDEA (Northeastern)
desc: Northeastern's student-led venture accelerator with gap funding up to $10K.
why: Equity-free gap funding and coaching, run by students for students.

name: C10 Labs
desc: AI-native venture studio and fund at CIC in Kendall Square â€” invests pre-seed to Series A and co-builds applied-AI companies; runs the AI BioHub with LabCentral and a Dimensional AI Hub with CIC.
why: A venture-studio path: trade some ownership for hands-on company building, with dedicated tracks for AI-in-bio and enterprise AI.
facts: Applied AI; AI-bio and enterprise tracks

name: Founder Institute Boston
desc: Global pre-seed accelerator's Boston chapter. Four-month program for idea-stage to early-traction founders, with a paid entrance fee and a 2.5% equity warrant pledged about two-thirds of the way through rather than at enrollment.
why: A structured first step for founders not yet ready for Techstars or MassChallenge â€” but note it charges an entrance fee, and the equity warrant activates once you raise $100K or more.

name: Auxilium Worcester
desc: Worcester innovation studio and accelerator backed by the Rucker Investments family office since June 2025. The accelerator invests $250K per company; pitched at two to three cohorts a year, only two have run (June 2025; June 2026 with Massachusetts Biomedical Initiatives (MBI) on life sciences). A studio residency adds up to $100K. Applications are closed and by invitation as of October 2026.
why: A first institutional check plus a free 24/7 desk for founders who will build in Central Massachusetts, and AI is explicitly in scope. It is full-time and on-site at 311 Main St, so expect to relocate for the program; cohorts to date have skewed to healthcare and medtech.
facts: Broad incl. AI, medtech; no drug development

name: VentureWell
desc: Nonprofit founded 1995 as the NCIIA, renamed 2014; long based in Hadley, now listed in downtown Amherst. E-Team grants US student invention teams up to $25K non-dilutive, plus training; Aspire and Ascend are five- and six-week investor-readiness programs for pre-seed and seed-stage science and engineering startups nationwide. Ran ARPA-H's Investor Catalyst Hub in Cambridge, Sept 2023â€“Feb 2026.
why: Equity-free money and a national investor-mentor bench for university-born hardware, medtech and applied-AI teams: $5K Pioneer, then $20K Propel, and the Summer 2026 cohort included several AI-powered devices. Programs are national rather than Boston-local, and E-Team requires currently enrolled students plus a faculty advisor.

name: BUILD617
desc: Founder-led community for early-stage tech founders in Boston and Cambridge, started by Nathan Spielberg (Tamarin AI) and Nick Leonard (VoiceRun). Founder dinners, tactical sessions and a podcast, plus a free workspace in Downtown Crossing opened in September 2026 with the real-estate firm Synergy. Membership skews heavily to AI companies.
why: Free desks and a peer group that takes no equity â€” but it selects for AI-native startups, expects you in three days a week, and asks companies to move on past eight employees. The space is sponsor-funded and committed for a year.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Machine Intelligence Community
desc: Harvard's flagship undergraduate AI/ML club â€” runs the Future of Intelligence Fellowship, an AI project incubator, tech talks and workshops.
why: Where Harvard's technical AI undergrads congregate â€” recruit a co-founder or your first engineer.

name: Tufts AI Society
desc: Tufts' primary student AI organization â€” hands-on workshops from neural networks to prompt engineering, semester project showcases and cross-campus AI mixers.
why: The AI talent pool on the Medford campus, and a bridge into Tufts' CS and robotics research community.

name: MIT Sandbox
desc: MIT's university-run venture program â€” up to $25K in non-dilutive funding, mentorship and startup education for any MIT student team, across every discipline.
why: Free money and structured mentorship before you've even incorporated â€” the widest on-ramp into MIT's startup pipeline.

name: eTower (Babson)
desc: Babson's live-in entrepreneurship community â€” 21 residents and 250+ alumni whose startups have raised $50M+, with an open Wednesday-night speaker series.
why: The weekly open speaker night is a standing invitation â€” founders and investors show up at a dorm in Wellesley because the community is that good.

name: Boston AI Week
desc: Statewide AI festival built from independently hosted events â€” talks, workshops, demo nights and hackathons â€” with Boston's Seaport as the hub neighborhood. The 2026 run is Sept 16 to Oct 28, with a core week Sept 24 to Oct 2. Free to attend, and most individual events are free. The 2025 edition drew 15,000+ participants to 125+ events.
why: The week the whole Massachusetts AI ecosystem is in one place â€” plan launches, hiring and investor meetings around it. Any Massachusetts host can list an event on the official calendar for free, approved on a rolling basis, so you can run your own demo night inside the program.
applyNote: Host an event: free listing, rolling

name: Massachusetts AI Coalition
desc: Private-sector coalition of Massachusetts AI founders, operators, investors and students, launched February 2026. Not an incubator or accelerator: it runs a free founder coworking space donated by Wayfair, a resource pack of compute credits and warm intros, a customer-pilot program with member companies, and a year-round event calendar.
why: If you are committed to building in Massachusetts, the Founder Starter Pack is the concrete ask: a free desk, GPU and cloud credits and warm intros, with no equity or fees. The pilot program pitches startups to member companies as first paying customers; quarterly Founder Rooms put founders in front of pledged angels.
facts: No equity, no fees; pack sent within 7 days
